experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Explore over 200km of groomed ski runs across Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. Suitable for all skill levels including beginners and children, with ski school options available for the whole family. Iconic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks make this an unforgettable alpine experience.

experiences.name: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Fiesch
experiences.description: A thrilling family-friendly activity where kids and adults race down dedicated snow tubing lanes and traditional sled runs. The Fiesch area offers gentle slopes perfect for younger children alongside faster runs for teens and adults, making it an ideal full-day family outing without requiring ski experience.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Excursion
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, walk on the glacier, and enjoy panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier. A magical experience for the entire family that combines culture, science, and breathtaking alpine scenery.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Enjoy a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Sample regional specialties including raclette, rösti, and local Valais wines or hot chocolate for the kids. Many chalets offer live folk music and a warm, authentic atmosphere that captures the heart of Swiss alpine culture.

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing and Winter Hiking at Lenzerheide
experiences.description: Discover 100km of groomed cross-country ski trails and scenic winter hiking paths through snow-covered pine forests. Lenzerheide offers dedicated family trails with gentle terrain, warming huts along the route, and stunning views of the Heidsee lake. A perfect low-intensity alternative to downhill skiing for mixed-ability families.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly SBB Swiss train from Zurich Airport to Grindelwald (approx. 2.5–3 hrs via Interlaken Ost, ~CHF 50–60 with a Swiss Travel Pass or half-fare card). Check in to Grindelwald Boutique Stay. Take a short orientation stroll through Grindelwald village, admire the iconic Eiger North Face views, and locate the nearest ski rental shops for tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the accommodation, unpack, and rest after travel. Take a gentle evening walk along the village main street to get familiar with local amenities, supermarkets (Migros or Coop for budget grocery shopping), and ski pass offices.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 8–12 for a sandwich and coffee).
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite at Zurich HB train station — try the Migros or Coop supermarket food counters for a sandwich or hot meal (CHF 8–12).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from Grindelwald's Coop or Migros supermarket. Stock up on pasta, bread, cheese, and local cold cuts. Cook a simple meal at the accommodation (CHF 10–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Jungfrau Region ski pass on arrival or online in advance — multi-day passes offer the best value. Consider purchasing a Swiss Half-Fare Card (CHF 120) if you plan multiple train journeys, as it halves most rail fares. Rent ski equipment from local shops like Buri Sport or Interlaken Sport for budget rates (CHF 30–45/day for skis, boots, and poles).

day_by_day.morning: Early start — pick up pre-booked ski rental equipment from a Grindelwald village shop (open from 08:00). Head to the First ski area (accessible via the First Gondola from the village center). Enjoy beginner-to-intermediate ski runs on the wide, well-groomed pistes of First. The First area is ideal for families with varied terrain for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at First. Take a lunch break at a mid-mountain restaurant or pack your own sandwiches from the supermarket to save money. After lunch, explore the gentler blue runs with younger family members or try the toboggan run at First for a fun non-ski alternative (toboggan rental ~CHF 10).
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment or store it at the rental shop. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a village café. Relax at the accommodation and prepare for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at accommodation — muesli, yogurt, bread, and jam purchased from Coop/Migros (CHF 3–5 per person).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from the accommodation — sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, and a thermos of hot tea (CHF 3–5 per person). Alternatively, grab a Wurst (sausage) from a mountain kiosk (~CHF 6–8).
meals.dinner: Try Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald village — a local favorite with hearty Swiss rösti, raclette, and fondue at moderate prices (CHF 18–28 per main). Share dishes to reduce costs.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfrau Ski Region Top Ski Pass covers First, Grindelwald-Wengen, Männlichen, and Kleine Scheidegg areas. A 6-day adult pass costs approximately CHF 290–330 — buy online in advance for discounts. Children under 9 ski free with a paying adult. Dress in warm layers as February temperatures at First can drop to -10°C to -5°C.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Grindelwald-Wengen cogwheel train (included in ski pass) to Kleine Scheidegg — one of the most scenic train rides in the Alps. Begin skiing the famous Lauberhorn slopes, home of the world's longest downhill ski race course. The wide open runs here are spectacular for intermediate skiers and families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski from Kleine Scheidegg down to Wengen village via the Lauberhorn runs. Explore Wengen — a charming car-free Alpine village. Let the kids enjoy the free sledging area near Wengen village. Take the cogwheel train back to Grindelwald in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Grindelwald's public outdoor ice skating rink (if open — check local schedules, entry ~CHF 5–8 including skate rental). A fun family winter activity that doesn't break the budget.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation — scrambled eggs, toast, and fruit (CHF 3–5 per person).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Kleine Scheidegg restaurant area — try the self-service section for a budget bowl of soup and bread (~CHF 12–16). Alternatively, bring packed snacks.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation — cook a hearty Swiss-style pasta with cheese sauce or a simple raclette using a portable raclette set (available at Coop). Budget CHF 8–12 per person for groceries.

day_by_day.notes: The cogwheel train between Grindelwald and Kleine Scheidegg is a highlight in itself — sit on the right side for the best Eiger views. Wengen is car-free and very family-friendly. Bring sunscreen as UV radiation is intense at altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Männlichen cable car from Grindelwald Grund (short walk or free shuttle from village). Ski the sunny, wide Männlichen plateau — excellent for families and beginners. Enjoy panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Try the famous 'Royal Walk' easy ski route along the ridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski down from Männlichen to Wengen or Grindelwald Grund via long, leisurely blue and red runs. For non-skiers or younger children, try the Männlichen winter hiking trail (free with ski pass) — a stunning 30-minute easy walk along the ridge with unbeatable Alpine views.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Grindelwald village. Visit the Grindelwald Sports Center for a swim or sauna session (entry ~CHF 8–12) — a great way to soothe tired ski muscles. Perfect family relaxation activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation — porridge with honey and dried fruit, coffee (CHF 2–4 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch again — this is the single biggest budget-saving tip on the mountain. Bring thermos soup, sandwiches, and chocolate (CHF 3–5 per person).
meals.dinner: Try Restaurant Firestarter in Grindelwald — known for good-value burgers, pizzas, and local dishes in a relaxed atmosphere (CHF 16–24 per main). Great for families.

day_by_day.notes: The Männlichen cable car from Grindelwald Grund is one of the longest cable car rides in Europe at 6.2 km — thrilling for kids! Check the Jungfrau Region website for any family ski lesson packages which can be booked for CHF 35–50 per child per half-day through the Swiss Ski School.

day_by_day.morning: Splurge day — take the Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' train excursion. Depart from Grindelwald Grund or Kleine Scheidegg on the famous cogwheel railway to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m. This is the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and enjoy breathtaking snow-covered views. Book tickets in advance for discounts (approx. CHF 145–165 for adults, CHF 72 for children 6–15, free under 6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at Jungfraujoch — try snow tubing and sledging on the plateau (free once at the top), visit the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven shop, and take iconic photos with the Aletsch Glacier — the longest glacier in the Alps. Begin descent by 15:00 to avoid crowds on the return train.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by 17:00. Rest and reflect on the day's highlights. Light evening activity — browse the village souvenir shops for affordable Swiss chocolates and postcards.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty self-prepared breakfast before departure — eggs, cheese, bread, and coffee (CHF 3–5 per person). Eat well as mountain food is expensive.
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch in a well-insulated bag for the Jungfraujoch visit — sandwiches, chocolate, and hot drinks in a thermos. Eating at the Jungfraujoch restaurants is very expensive (CHF 25–40 per meal). Self-catering saves CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Treat yourselves to a proper Swiss fondue dinner at Restaurant Chalet Egg in Grindelwald — a cozy, authentic experience. Cheese fondue costs ~CHF 28–35 per person. Share a pot between two to reduce cost.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance at jungfrau.ch — 'Good Morning Tickets' (departing before 08:00) offer significant discounts of 20–30%. Dress extremely warmly — temperatures at the top can be -15°C to -20°C with wind chill. The altitude can cause mild headaches — take it slow and stay hydrated. This is the one 'splurge' day of the trip but absolutely unmissable.

day_by_day.morning: Final full ski day — return to your favorite ski area (First or Kleine Scheidegg recommended). Focus on perfecting runs you enjoyed during the week. Families can try a guided family ski lesson through the Swiss Ski School for a group session (CHF 35–50 per child, CHF 45–60 per adult for a half-day group lesson). Great for building confidence on the last ski day.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skiing, try the Grindelwald First Cliff Walk — a spectacular free-to-access suspension bridge and cliff path at First mountain station (accessible via gondola, gondola ticket ~CHF 20 return if not using ski pass). The cliff walk offers jaw-dropping views over the valley and is suitable for children over 5.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski celebration! Head to a village bar or café for a budget-friendly drink — try a local Swiss beer (CHF 5–7) or warm Glühwein (mulled wine, CHF 5–6). Pack ski rental equipment to return tomorrow morning.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation — use up remaining groceries. Toast, cheese, yogurt, and fruit (CHF 2–4 per person).
meals.lunch: Last mountain packed lunch — use remaining sandwich supplies and snacks from the accommodation (CHF 3–5 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Pizzeria Avocado in Grindelwald — good-value pizzas and pasta in a family-friendly setting (CHF 15–22 per main). A relaxed and affordable way to celebrate the final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Return ski rental equipment first thing tomorrow morning to avoid extra charges. Check accommodation checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed. Saturday is typically busier on the slopes — head out early (before 09:00) to beat the weekend crowds. Buy Swiss chocolate and local cheese at Coop as affordable, high-quality souvenirs (CHF 5–15).

day_by_day.morning: Return ski rental equipment to the shop (open from 08:00). Check out of Grindelwald Boutique Stay. Store luggage at the accommodation or train station if you have time to spare. Take a final scenic walk through Grindelwald village — photograph the Eiger one last time and visit the small Grindelwald Museum (entry ~CHF 5) for a brief overview of Alpine history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Grindelwald by train toward Interlaken Ost and onward to Zurich Airport. The journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours. If time permits before the train, stop in Interlaken for 30–45 minutes — stroll along the Höheweg promenade between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz for stunning final Alpine views at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport for departure. Grab a final Swiss meal at the airport — try the Coop or Migros airport outlets for an affordable sandwich or hot meal (CHF 10–15) before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared or grab-and-go breakfast from Coop in Grindelwald — yogurt, pastry, and coffee to take on the train (CHF 5–8 per person).
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Interlaken Ost station or on the train — packed snacks or a station bakery item (CHF 6–10 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Zurich Airport — Coop or Migros food court for a budget-friendly final Swiss meal (CHF 10–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Validate your train tickets before boarding — Swiss trains require ticket validation. If you purchased a Swiss Travel Pass, it covers the full return journey to Zurich Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Zurich Airport. Zurich Airport is extremely efficient — 90 minutes is the minimum but 2.5 hours is recommended for international flights. Ensure ski equipment is properly packed if bringing it home — oversized baggage fees apply with most airlines.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival – Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activity scheduled. Rest and travel from the airport to Grindelwald via train (approx. 2.5–3 hrs from Zurich Airport via Interlaken Ost). Enjoy the scenic rail journey through the Swiss countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Grindelwald Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to get your bearings. Visit the local sports rental shop to book ski equipment and lift passes for the coming days. Pick up a trail map and plan the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a cozy local restaurant in Grindelwald village. Explore the charming alpine streets and get an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or grab a snack at Zurich Airport before boarding the train.
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich from a bakery or café at Interlaken Ost station during the transfer.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Firestarter or Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald – hearty Swiss classics like rösti, alpine pasta, and local beer. Budget approx. CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book ski rentals online (e.g., Intersport Grindelwald) to save time and get better rates. Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass can offer significant savings on trains and lifts — purchase in advance online. Grindelwald is about 2.5–3 hours from Zurich Airport by train.

day_by_day.morning: First ski day on the Jungfrau Region Slopes! Head to the Grindelwald-First gondola (a 5-minute walk from the village center) and access over 200km of groomed runs. Beginners can stick to the gentle blue runs near First, while more experienced skiers can tackle the red and black runs down to Grindelwald. Ski from approximately 09:00–12:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau slopes, this time exploring the Männlichen area accessible via the Grindelwald Terminal gondola. Enjoy the wide, family-friendly runs with panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Ski until approximately 15:30, then return equipment if renting daily or head back to the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel, enjoy a warm drink by the fire, and freshen up. Head out for dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the boutique hotel or a nearby café such as Café 3692 – enjoy Swiss bread, cheese, cold cuts, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at the First Cliff Walk Restaurant or Bergrestaurant Männlichen – try the daily soup, alpine macaroni (Älplermagronen), or a warm sandwich. Budget CHF 18–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Kirchbühl's restaurant or Gasthof Glacier in Grindelwald – try the beef fondue or a hearty mountain platter. Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a multi-day Jungfrau Ski Region pass (available for 2–13 days) for the best value. The Jungfrau Travel Pass also covers public transport between resorts. Dress in moisture-wicking layers and apply high-SPF sunscreen — alpine sun reflects strongly off snow even in February.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Excursion! Depart from Grindelwald Grund station at approximately 08:30 on the cogwheel train via Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and enjoy breathtaking views over the Aletsch Glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — try the snow activities on the plateau (short sledding runs, photo opportunities with huskies, or simply walk on the glacier). Begin the descent back to Grindelwald by approximately 14:00–15:00. Stop at Kleine Scheidegg on the way back for a break and panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience! Book a traditional cheese fondue dinner at a mountain chalet restaurant — a perfect cultural and culinary highlight of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack a light snack for the train ride up.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Restaurant — enjoy a warm meal with incredible views. Budget CHF 25–40 per person. Alternatively, pack sandwiches to save costs.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner at Restaurant Chalet Egg or Fondue Stübli in Grindelwald — traditional cheese fondue with bread, pickles, and local white wine. Budget CHF 40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance online (jungfrau.ch) — tickets sell out fast in February. The round trip from Grindelwald costs approximately CHF 145–160 per adult (discounts with Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass). Dress in extra warm layers — temperatures at the summit can drop to -15°C or lower. Altitude sickness is possible; ascend slowly and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Fiesch — a fantastic family-friendly day! Travel from Grindelwald to Fiesch via train through Interlaken (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Arrive by 09:30 and spend the morning racing down dedicated snow tubing lanes and sledding runs. Suitable for all ages including young children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the fun at Fiesch — try different tubing lanes and explore the area. If time allows, take the Fiesch gondola up for scenic winter views over the Aletsch Glacier region. Head back toward Grindelwald by approximately 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening at the hotel — warm up in the hotel lounge, enjoy hot chocolate, and let the family rest after an active day. Light dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Fiesch resort café or restaurant — try a warm soup, grilled sausages (Bratwurst), and fries. Budget CHF 18–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a Grindelwald pizzeria or family-friendly restaurant such as Restaurant Alpenhof — pizza, pasta, and simple Swiss dishes. Budget CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Fiesch is a bit of a journey from Grindelwald — consider departing by 07:30–08:00 to maximize time there. Snow tubing tickets are typically CHF 15–25 per person for a session. Check the Fiesch resort website for opening hours and conditions before traveling. Alternatively, if the family prefers to stay local, Grindelwald-First also offers a dedicated sledding run.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing and Winter Hiking at Lenzerheide. Travel from Grindelwald to Lenzerheide (approx. 2–2.5 hrs by train and bus via Chur). Arrive by 09:30 and explore 100km of groomed cross-country ski trails. Beginners can rent equipment and take a short lesson, while experienced skiers can tackle longer loops through the snow-covered forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Switch to winter hiking along the scenic marked trails around Lenzerheide lake and surrounding woodland. The flat lakeside paths are perfect for families and offer stunning mountain panoramas. Return to Grindelwald by approximately 17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Grindelwald — browse the village shops for Swiss chocolates and souvenirs. Enjoy a sit-down dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Lenzerheide mountain restaurant — try the daily special (Tagesmenü) which typically includes soup, main course, and dessert at good value. Budget CHF 22–32 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Mercato or Pizzeria da Salvo in Grindelwald — a mix of Swiss and Italian dishes in a relaxed setting. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rentals at Lenzerheide are approximately CHF 25–35 per day. A cross-country ski trail pass is typically CHF 10–15 per adult. If the family prefers to stay in the Grindelwald area on this day, the Grindelwald-First Cliff Walk and local winter hiking trails are excellent alternatives — free to walk with appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Final ski day on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — make the most of your lift pass! Head to Wengen or Mürren for a change of scenery. Mürren is a car-free village accessible by cable car from Lauterbrunnen and offers dramatic views and excellent intermediate-to-advanced runs. Ski from 09:00–12:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Grindelwald by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at leisure — optional activities include ice skating at the Grindelwald Sports Centre (approx. CHF 10–15 per person), a spa visit at one of the local hotels, or a final snowshoe walk around the village perimeter.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at one of Grindelwald's best restaurants — a celebratory end to the Swiss Alps adventure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Winteregg near Mürren or a mountain hut on the slopes — try the cheese soup (Käsesuppe) and warm apple strudel. Budget CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Schmitte or the hotel's own restaurant — splurge slightly on a three-course meal featuring local specialties like Berner Platte, raclette, or venison stew. Budget CHF 50–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is one of the most scenic and charming ski villages in Switzerland — highly recommended as a day trip. To reach Mürren from Grindelwald: train to Lauterbrunnen, then cable car to Grütschalp, then train to Mürren (approx. 1 hr total). The Schilthorn (famous from the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service') is also accessible from Mürren for an optional detour.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Grindelwald. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the hotel. Take a short walk through the village for last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up Swiss chocolate (Lindt, Läderach, or local brands), cheese, and alpine gifts. Pack and check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Grindelwald by train toward the airport (Zurich or Geneva depending on your return flight). The scenic train journey back through the Bernese Oberland is a beautiful final memory of the Swiss Alps. Enjoy the views of the Eiger and the rolling countryside as you travel.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final meal at the airport or in Zurich city center if time allows.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — enjoy a leisurely Swiss spread of cheeses, meats, fresh bread, jams, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Grindelwald before departure, or grab a takeaway sandwich and Swiss chocolate for the train journey. Budget CHF 15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a quick meal in Zurich city center if time permits — try a traditional Swiss German restaurant near the Hauptbahnhof (main station) for a final rösti or schnitzel. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Train from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport takes approximately 2.5–3 hours via Interlaken Ost — plan to depart at least 3.5 hours before your flight. Validate all train tickets before boarding. Swiss trains are extremely punctual — arrive at the platform a few minutes early. Don't forget to claim VAT refunds on eligible purchases if you are a non-EU resident — collect receipts throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-transit)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and snacks arranged in the private transfer vehicle, or a quick arrival bite at a premium café in Grindelwald village upon check-in
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner at a top-rated mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald — multi-course fondue menu with regional cheeses, cured meats, artisan breads, and a curated Swiss wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. Confirm ski equipment rental or purchase appointments for Day 2. Tip: Grindelwald sits at ~1,034m — take it easy on Day 1 to acclimatize before hitting the slopes.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Begin your first full ski day on the world-class First ski area above Grindelwald. Access 200km+ of groomed pistes across all difficulty levels. A private ski instructor can be arranged for the family to assess skill levels and provide tailored coaching on the pristine morning snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Skiing — Head to the Kleine Scheidegg connecting area for breathtaking runs with panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Enjoy the quieter afternoon pistes and try intermediate blue and red runs. A mid-afternoon hot chocolate or Glühwein break at a premium mountain restaurant is highly recommended.
day_by_day.evening: Après-Ski & Gourmet Dinner — Return to the village for a relaxing après-ski session at the hotel's spa or lounge. Dine at one of Grindelwald's finest restaurants, such as the restaurant at the Grand Hotel Regina or Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof, featuring seasonal alpine cuisine with locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the boutique hotel featuring fresh pastries, Swiss cheeses, cold cuts, hot dishes, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Premium mountain restaurant lunch on the slopes — try Bergrestaurant Grindelwald First or Restaurant Brandegg, with panoramic Eiger views and hearty alpine dishes such as Rösti, Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, and fresh mountain soups
meals.dinner: Fine dining at a top Grindelwald restaurant — expect a 4-course menu featuring seasonal Swiss alpine cuisine, premium wine list, and impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: Book a certified private ski instructor through the hotel concierge or Grindelwald Ski School for a personalized family lesson. Ensure all family members have properly fitted ski rentals from a premium rental shop such as Buri Sport or Intersport Grindelwald.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Excursion — Board the iconic cogwheel train from Grindelwald Grund station for the spectacular ride up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and the vast Aletsch Glacier stretching into the distance. A truly unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jungfraujoch Continued & Descent — Enjoy lunch at the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven or Crystal Restaurant at the summit. Spend the afternoon exploring the snow plateau, trying the Snowboard Zipline or Snow Fun Park at the top, before descending on the cogwheel train back to Kleine Scheidegg, with optional skiing down to Grindelwald Grund.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed Spa Evening & Casual Dinner — After a high-altitude day, unwind with a luxurious spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby premium wellness center. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a cozy Grindelwald bistro or the hotel's own restaurant with lighter Swiss fare and a fine wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast at the hotel — fuel up before the high-altitude excursion with protein-rich options, fresh fruits, and hot beverages
meals.lunch: Lunch at the summit restaurants on Jungfraujoch — Crystal Restaurant offers warm meals with glacier views; alternatively, enjoy the self-service restaurant for a quicker bite between explorations
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a premium Grindelwald bistro or hotel restaurant — lighter alpine dishes such as mountain trout, veal, or vegetable Rösti, paired with Swiss Pinot Noir or Chasselas

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — the experience is extremely popular even in winter. Dress in extra warm layers as temperatures at the summit can drop to -15°C or below. The excursion typically takes 5–6 hours round trip. Children under 16 receive discounted train fares.

day_by_day.morning: Snow Tubing and Sledding at Fiesch — Enjoy a thrilling family day out at Fiesch, reachable by scenic train from Grindelwald. Race down dedicated snow tubing lanes and sledding runs in a safe, purpose-built facility. This is a perfect activity for all ages and skill levels, guaranteeing laughter and excitement for the entire family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Aletsch Arena Exploration — After tubing, explore the Aletsch Arena area. Opt for a guided snowshoe walk along the edge of the Aletsch Glacier with a private alpine guide, or enjoy a relaxed afternoon at the Fiesch village, browsing artisan shops and warming up in a local café with hot Swiss cocoa and pastries before returning to Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Private Chalet Dinner Experience — Arrange a private in-chalet or in-suite dining experience through your hotel concierge. A private chef prepares a bespoke multi-course Swiss and European menu exclusively for your family — an intimate and unforgettable luxury evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with a special packed snack bag prepared by the kitchen for the day trip to Fiesch
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mountain restaurant or café in Fiesch — hearty Swiss mountain fare including soups, Bratwurst, and warm apple strudel to refuel after tubing
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or chalet dinner prepared by a private chef — a bespoke multi-course menu with wine pairing, tailored to the family's preferences and dietary requirements

day_by_day.notes: Travel time from Grindelwald to Fiesch is approximately 1.5–2 hours by train via Interlaken and the Rhône Valley — arrange an early departure. Alternatively, hire a private luxury van for door-to-door convenience. Book the private chef experience at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Advanced Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes — Return to the slopes for a second dedicated ski day, this time exploring the Männlichen and Kleine Scheidegg areas. Take the Grindelwald–Männlichen gondola (one of the longest in Europe) for spectacular ridge skiing with 360° panoramic views. Push skill levels with more challenging red and black runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Family Ski Adventure & Ski Safari — Join a guided ski safari across the interconnected Jungfrau Ski Region, linking Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren across three valleys. A private guide leads the family through hidden routes and scenic off-piste-adjacent terrain, making it an adventure for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner — Round off the ski week's most active day with a second, more elaborate Swiss fondue and raclette dinner at a different premium mountain chalet restaurant. Try a Bacchus fondue (fondue with white wine) or a chocolate fondue dessert for a sweet finish to the evening.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast with energy-boosting options — eggs, smoked salmon, granola, and fresh alpine dairy products
meals.lunch: Slope-side lunch at Restaurant Männlichen or Berghaus Grindelwald First — panoramic terrace dining with views of the Bernese Alps and hearty ski-day classics
meals.dinner: Elaborate Swiss fondue and raclette dinner at a premium chalet restaurant — include a chocolate fondue dessert course and pair with a Fendant white wine from the Valais region

day_by_day.notes: The Männlichen gondola is one of Europe's longest cable car rides at 6.2km — a thrilling experience even before the first run. Book a private ski guide for the ski safari through the Grindelwald Ski School or a specialist alpine guiding company. Confirm Mürren access via the Lauterbrunnen–Grütschalp ferry and train if included.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing and Winter Hiking at Lenzerheide — Travel to the Lenzerheide resort area (approximately 2 hours by private transfer) to explore 100km of perfectly groomed cross-country ski trails. Hire a private cross-country ski instructor for the family and glide through breathtaking snow-covered pine forests and frozen lake landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Winter Hiking & Snowshoeing at Lenzerheide — Transition to a guided winter hiking or snowshoeing tour through the scenic Lenzerheide valley. The trails offer stunning views of the Heidsee lake and surrounding Graubünden peaks. A private alpine guide narrates the local flora, fauna, and mountain heritage along the route.
day_by_day.evening: Gourmet Dinner in Lenzerheide or Return & Farewell Pre-Dinner Drinks — Enjoy a premium dinner at one of Lenzerheide's celebrated restaurants, such as Valsana Hotel's Ustria Veglia, before a private transfer back to Grindelwald. Alternatively, return to Grindelwald for a sunset Glühwein toast on the hotel terrace with Eiger views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast to allow time for the transfer to Lenzerheide
meals.lunch: Lunch at a cozy cross-country ski lodge or mountain restaurant in Lenzerheide — warm soups, alpine cheese plates, and homemade breads
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Ustria Veglia or a comparable premium Lenzerheide restaurant featuring Graubünden regional specialties such as Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), Capuns, and Maluns, with an extensive Swiss wine list

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury vehicle for the Lenzerheide day trip for maximum comfort and flexibility. Cross-country skiing is a lower-impact alternative for family members who may need a rest from downhill skiing. Book cross-country ski rentals and instructor in advance through Lenzerheide's ski school.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning Ski Run or Leisure Activity — Enjoy a final leisurely ski run on the Grindelwald–First slopes, savoring the views one last time. Alternatively, families who prefer a rest day can enjoy a late breakfast followed by a private guided ice skating session on a local rink, or a relaxing morning at the hotel spa with a signature alpine wellness treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Village Exploration & Souvenir Shopping — Spend the final afternoon exploring Grindelwald village at a leisurely pace. Visit artisan shops for Swiss chocolates, watches, and alpine crafts. Stop at a premium chocolatier for a bespoke chocolate tasting and to pick up gifts. Begin packing and hotel check-out preparations.
day_by_day.evening: Grand Farewell Dinner — Celebrate the final evening with a lavish farewell dinner at Grindelwald's finest restaurant. Opt for a chef's tasting menu with wine pairing — a curated journey through Swiss alpine gastronomy featuring seasonal ingredients, artisan cheeses, and premium Swiss and European wines. Toast to an unforgettable alpine adventure.

meals.breakfast: Extended, indulgent hotel breakfast — a leisurely final morning feast with all premium offerings including Swiss pastries, artisan cheeses, smoked fish, and Champagne mimosas
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Grindelwald village café or hotel lounge — sandwiches, soups, and hot drinks to keep energy up for afternoon activities
meals.dinner: Grand farewell tasting menu dinner at Grindelwald's top fine dining restaurant — 6-course chef's menu with Swiss alpine produce, artisan cheese board, chocolate dessert, and a premium wine pairing curated by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer for departure on the following day if flying out on Day 8, or confirm same-day transfer timing if departing on the evening of Day 7. Allow at least 3–3.5 hours travel time to Zurich Airport and 4 hours to Geneva Airport. Settle any outstanding hotel charges and tip service staff appropriately as a gesture of appreciation for a premium experience.
